name: Windmill Growth
description: Done-for-you personal branding / LinkedIn content service for B2B founders (~$3,999/mo retainers).

mentions.evidence: ~$111.7k MRR, 79 active subscriptions, ~$113k L30, ~$2.17M all-time, bootstrapped, founded May 2024. Last sync Sep 29, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Service-as-SaaS billing at ~$4k/seat — fewer customers, real cash, if you can deliver LinkedIn output consistently.

whyItPrints: High ACV service wrapped in Stripe subscriptions — founders hate posting, Windmill sells the relief. Ops-heavy, not product-sexy.
whyThisMatters:
They write LinkedIn for B2B founders, and they post it too. The process on the site is short. You talk for 45 minutes. They write the posts, publish them, work the audience, and try to fill the calendar. The promise up top is that it shouldn't sound like a model wrote it. The part they say they won't touch is how you actually sound.

They take the whole account. Not a draft you then have to paste yourself. Strategy, writing, posting, replies. It's a service with a monthly bill, which is why it shows up next to software companies even though the work is people writing posts. They're selling the relief of not being the one who has to post.

Under that pitch, named case studies. Real founders, their companies, results those people tie back to LinkedIn. Specific accounts, not a wall of logos you can't check.

You book a strategy call. There's a pricing page, some articles, an FAQ. A call fits a retainer better than a signup box. One retainer is a conversation, a voice, a posting schedule, and the replies.
